title: Strict-henselization stalk formula
statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], let $F\in\Ab(X_{\Et})$ be a torsion abelian etale sheaf [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], and let $\bar s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$ be a geometric point. Put $S_{(\bar s)}=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{S,\bar s}$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], let $p:X\times_SS_{(\bar s)}\to X$ be the projection, and use the higher direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], geometric stalk [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], and etale cohomology [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. Then the canonical restriction map is an isomorphism for every $q\geq0$:

$$
 (R^qf_*F)_{\bar s}\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q((X\times_SS_{(\bar s)})_{\Et},p^{-1}F).
$$

For $K\in D^+(\Ab(X_{\Et}))$ [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories] with torsion cohomology sheaves, the corresponding canonical map is an isomorphism in $D^+(\Ab)$:

$$
 (Rf_*K)_{\bar s}\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma((X\times_SS_{(\bar s)})_{\Et},p^{-1}K).
$$

proof.text: For the ordinary sheaf clause apply [lem-weil-pbc-unrestricted-strict-henselization-stalk] directly to f, s, F and q; its conclusion is the identical canonical map without requiring the torsion hypothesis. For the derived clause choose the unique germ restriction r by [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-restriction]. It is invertible by [lem-weil-pbc-strict-local-germ-restriction-iso]. The global-sections image of homology of the derived base-change mate is invertible by [lem-weil-pbc-strict-local-base-change-global-homology]. The inverse-image/homology comparison and strict-local Leray comparison are isomorphisms by their definitions. Composition proves the displayed canonical derived clause in every degree.

proof_origin.place: Tags 03Q9 and 03QO, separating germ identification from global homology of the base-change mate

blueprint_sketch.statement:
For quasi-compact quasi-separated $f:X\to S$, torsion $F$, and $q\geq0$,

$$
(R^qf_*F)_{\bar s}\cong
H^q(X\times_SS_{(\bar s)},F|).
$$

For $K\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}})$ this lifts to

$$
(Rf_*K)_{\bar s}\xrightarrow{\sim}
R\Gamma(X\times_SS_{(\bar s)},K|)
$$

in $D^+(\mathbf{Ab})$.
blueprint_sketch.proof:
The stalk is the colimit over $\mathcal N_{\bar s}^{\mathrm{op}}$ of
$H^q(X\times_SV,F|)$. Replace the index by affine neighbourhoods, identify
their inverse limit by Lemma [lemma-weil-pbc-fibre-product-limit], and
apply cohomology continuity. For the derived statement, choose a
bounded-below injective complex $J^\bullet$ representing $K$. The chain map
from the stalk complex $(f_*J^\bullet)_{\bar s}$ to the sections complex on
the strict henselization is obtained by restricting each representative
section. Its map on every cohomology group is the preceding isomorphism, so
it is a quasi-isomorphism. This expands Tag `03Q9`.
